channel.title: North Wales Chronicle - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from North Wales Chronicle (northwaleschronicle.co.uk)

item.title: Aldi apologises and offers refund after 'traumatised' shopper found starfish in meal
item.description: Aldi apologised for the "unexpected guests she found", which they claim are common starfish and not harmful, and provided a full refund.

item.title: New documentary celebrates 150 years of football in Bangor
item.description: The Welsh-language documentary Ni ’Di Bangor, Aye! explores the decline and revival of football in Bangor as the city celebrates 150 years of the sport

item.title: North Wales company expecting £3m sales boost from trade fair
item.description: Harlech Foodservice forecasts £3m sales at Expo 26 in Llandudno, with 3,000 buyers and 115 suppliers, including major UK and Welsh food brands. Expansion news.

item.title: Musical performance at care home set to be taken on overseas tour
item.description: Dawns i Bawb marked its 30th anniversary with a lively show at Bryn Seiont Newydd care home, Caernarfon, bringing music, dance and joy to residents.

item.title: Bangor manufacturer reaches new heights with multi-million pound export deals
item.description: The company’s recent success has been led by five new, multi-year agreements in Europe, worth a combined €13million, or £11.3million.

item.title: Direct post-match train service from Cardiff to North Wales to be trialled
item.description: A dedicated train service to North Wales from Cardiff will be trialled following Wales’ World Cup play-off fixtures in March.

item.title: Michael Sheen delivers a magnificent performance in Our Town
item.description: Michael Sheen’s return to the Welsh stage in the Welsh National Theatre’s inaugural production of Our Town is nothing short of a masterstroke.

item.title: Bala developer wins approval for 48 new homes on outskirts of Bangor
item.description: The project also features gardens, pedestrian and vehicle access, parking, play areas, and landscaping.

item.title: 'Support is available' as council tax to be hiked by 5.17% in Gwynedd
item.description: People in Gwynedd face a 5.17% rise in their council tax bills as the authority moves to protect key services amid rising demand and inflationary pressures.

item.title: Police insist 'case still open' 23 years on from murder of postman Paul Savage
item.description: It is now 23 years since postman Paul Savage was murdered in Mold.
